mfg1-mechanical-lesson-085.title: Identify lathe holding parts and feed-related components
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-085.objective: Identify lathe holding parts and feed-related components, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: The headstock relates to the spindle and other parts rotating the workpiece; the chuck grips the workpiece. The tailstock supports it from the opposite side and serves related purposes. The tool post holds the cutting tool, while the carriage, saddle and related parts move the tool. When learning names, use a diagram to distinguish which parts hold or move the workpiece or tool.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Soft jaws are relatively soft chuck jaws used to grip a workpiece, sometimes machined to fit it. Having chuck jaws does not mean every shape can be held safely. Fitting and jaw machining require appropriate training and approved methods. Do not check contact by hand during operation.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Part names help specify an abnormality’s location, but identifying a part does not authorize disassembly or adjustment. On a paper machine diagram, match the headstock, chuck, tool post, tailstock and carriage to their positions and roles. Ask the instructor about differences between actual machine models.

terms.meaning: The machine part associated with the spindle and related components.
Relatively soft jaws machined to suit workpiece holding.
The part supporting a workpiece or similar object from the opposite side.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-086.title: Compare the structures of milling machines, drill presses and machining centers
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-086.objective: Compare the structures of milling machines, drill presses and machining centers, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: A milling machine’s spindle-mounted tool rotates, machining through movement relative to the table carrying the workpiece and related parts. The bed and column support the machine; the spindle head and spindle relate to the tool side. For a drill press, organize the roles of the drill, chuck, column, table and base.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: A machining center can change tools automatically. In the source’s examples, a vertical machine has a vertical spindle for operations such as top-face machining; a horizontal machine can use a rotary table and related arrangements to machine several faces without refixturing. The words vertical or horizontal alone do not prove that every part or face can be machined.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: When selecting a process, match the required face, tool-access direction, holding and equipment capability. Knowing part names in a drawing is separate from the training needed to move a table or change a tool in practice. Draw machining faces and tool directions on paper and practice reading the process sheet.

terms.meaning: A column-shaped part supporting the spindle head and related components.

terms.reading: こうぐじどうこうかん
terms.meaning: A function by which the machine changes tools automatically.
A rotatable table that changes workpiece orientation.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-087.title: Organize grinding-wheel and chip hazards by process
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-087.objective: Organize grinding-wheel and chip hazards by process, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: A grinder’s wheel rotates at high speed, and cracks or fractures can cause fragments to fly. Follow the specified training and procedures for pre-use inspection, fitting and trial runs. Appearance alone does not prove safety; ask the responsible person about uncertainty or abnormalities. Whether a wheel’s side may be used also depends on the tool’s specification.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Chips from lathes and similar machines are sharp and may be hot. After stopping and checking safety, clear them with the specified brush or other tool, not bare hands. Grinding removes material with abrasive grains; polishing uses paste-like abrasives and related materials to finish the surface. A shiny polished surface does not prove that hazardous chips or dimensional defects have disappeared.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Welding involves intense light, heat, fumes and gases; casting involves hot molten metal and tools. In plastic working, a press shapes with force, forging uses blows and related forces, and rolling uses rolls. Match each process name with its hazards. One pair of gloves or protective glasses cannot be assumed to prevent every hazard.

terms.meaning: A tool using abrasive grains to remove material.
Metal in a molten state.
A material used to polish a surface.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-088.title: Organize five resin-forming methods and solidification by process
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-088.objective: Organize five resin-forming methods and solidification by process, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Injection molding puts flowing resin into a mold. Blow molding introduces air into a tube-shaped or similar material to form a hollow shape against the mold. Extrusion continuously pushes material through a die to make long products of the same cross-section. A hollow tube is not necessarily blow-molded.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Compression molding presses material inside a mold; the source gives thermosetting resins, rubber and related examples. In the reinforced-plastic example, resin impregnates glass fibers or another reinforcement, rollers remove air, and a chemical reaction integrates the material. Reinforcement is not foreign matter to be removed wholesale.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Materials that solidify by cooling and those that cure through reaction have different completion conditions. Producing a shape does not permit omitting cooling, curing, removal and inspection. Organize candidate methods from cross-section, material, how it solidifies and quantity. Actual temperature, pressure and composition follow approved instructions.

terms.reading: ねつこうかせいじゅし
terms.meaning: A resin curing by a chemical reaction through heat and related causes.
A material combined with another to supplement its properties.
Becoming hard through chemical reaction or similar processes.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-089.title: Compare electrostatic painting and electrodeposition coating
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-089.objective: Compare electrostatic painting and electrodeposition coating, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Brushing or rolling paint across a surface differs from spraying atomized paint. Uniform-looking color does not by itself establish that either method meets requirements for the substrate, target face, thickness, drying and other conditions. Check the specified product and paint.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Electrostatic painting uses electrical force to attract charged paint particles to a product. The source explains product grounding and paint charging. Electrodeposition coating puts the product into a paint-containing bath and uses electricity to form the film. A bath process is different from attracting particles flying through space.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Connect the required functions—corrosion protection, appearance, insulation or heat shielding—to process requirements. Follow specified grounding, ventilation, suitable protection and other conditions for equipment using electricity and chemicals. Understanding the principle does not authorize changing bath conditions, supply or paint independently.

terms.meaning: Entering a state of carrying electric charge.
Coating that forms a paint film using electricity in a bath.
A film of paint formed on a surface.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-090.title: Compare hot and cold rolling through their benefits, constraints and later processes
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-090.objective: Compare hot and cold rolling through their benefits, constraints and later processes, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: At high temperatures, hot-rolled material deforms more readily, with examples of substantial deformation using relatively less force. Cooling causes shrinkage, so dimensions and oxidation films formed by air reactions need checking. Consider heating energy too. Hot rolling does not make surface and dimensional checks unnecessary.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Cold rolling can provide dimensional accuracy and surface finish, but needs greater force and may cause work hardening. Check the process sheet for annealing and other post-treatment as needed. Confusing annealing with quenching changes the treatment’s purpose, so match the name and requirement.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Rolling oil helps adjust friction, remove heat and suppress seizure or scratches. Check thickness, surface, strength and other requirements including later surface treatment and property adjustment. Not heating does not mean there is no roll-entanglement hazard or process heat. Check equipment and product conditions from the specified safe area.

terms.meaning: A film formed on a surface by oxidation.
Hardening caused by plastic working.
A state of strong surface adhesion and damage from friction and related causes.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-091.title: Trace aluminum-extrusion processes and product features
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-091.objective: Trace aluminum-extrusion processes and product features, explaining the target, principles and conditions to check.

paragraphs.title: Target and role
paragraphs.text: Aluminum extrusion links billet heating, pushing through a die, cooling, straightening, cutting and related steps. The source gives a heating example around 400–500°C, not a workplace setpoint for every material. Too low a temperature can increase load; too high a temperature can cause cracks and other problems. Follow approved conditions combining material, shape and speed.

paragraphs.title: Principles and distinctions
paragraphs.text: Examples include window sashes, door frames, structural members and heat-dissipation parts with fins. A sash may have a complex inner and outer shape. Fins increase surface area to help release heat. A continuing cross-section and satisfaction of required strength or surface quality are checked separately.

paragraphs.title: Records and checks
paragraphs.text: Die scratches, dirt and adhered metal, as well as debris on the runout table, are candidates when investigating lengthwise lines or surface scratches. Before-and-after inspections, cleaning and repair follow the responsible personnel’s procedure. Do not reach into a table while the machine moves or hold a hot product by hand to investigate a cause.

terms.meaning: A block of metal stock used for extrusion and similar processes.
Bringing bends and related features into the specified state.
A thin projection provided to increase surface area and serve related purposes.
